newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf Petrochemical operating profit falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Petrochemical operating profit falls sharply.

text.p: Gulf Petrochemical Industries Co (GPIC) said on Wednesday it made a $52 million operating profit in 1996, down 42.2 percent on the previous year's $90 million.
A GPIC statement did not give net profit or a reason for the drop in operating profit, but said it produced 777,000 tonnes of ammonia and methanol in 1996, down from 862,000 tonnes in 1995.
The Bahrain-based GPIC is owned by the Bahrain National Oil Co, Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp and Kuwait's Petrochemical Industries Co.
GPIC is building a new 1,700-tonne per day urea plant in Bahrain.
It signed a $136 million contract in 1995 with Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd to build the plant and associated facilities.
